query: What travel policy risks appear in expense descriptions?

per_column.name: expense_type_label
per_column.rationale: Classifies the expense into categories (asset registration, travel, etc.). This is a descriptive attribute of the expense that may correlate with risk, but it is not itself an aspect/part OF travel policy risk. A travel expense is not a facet of the risk concept.

per_column.name: travel_item_hardware_mismatch
per_column.rationale: Whether an item claimed under travel does not match travel context (e.g., hardware billed as travel) is a genuine constitutive dimension of policy risk -- a misclassification/mismatch aspect of the violation itself.

per_column.name: personal_vs_business_ambiguity
per_column.rationale: Ambiguity over whether an expense is personal or business is a core sub-aspect of travel policy risk (personal-use violations), representing a distinct part of the risk concept.

per_column.name: ci_name_anomaly
per_column.rationale: An anomaly in the configuration-item name is a generic data-quality/anomaly signal. It may hint at irregularity but is not an aspect that constitutes travel policy risk specifically.

per_column.name: source_id_present
per_column.rationale: Mere presence of a source_id is a metadata completeness flag, not a constitutive aspect of travel policy risk.

per_column.name: processing_lag_risk
per_column.rationale: Processing latency is an operational/workflow attribute. It is a possible external indicator of control weakness but not a part-of travel policy risk itself.

per_column.name: entry_method
per_column.rationale: How an entry was created (manual/auto) is a provenance attribute that may predict error, not a constitutive facet of the risk concept.

per_column.name: department_travel_alignment
per_column.rationale: Whether a travel expense aligns with the department's expected travel profile captures an unauthorized/unexpected-travel aspect, a genuine sub-dimension of travel policy risk.

judge.rationale: Only three of eight added columns are true constitutive facets of travel_policy_risk (item/hardware mismatch, personal-vs-business ambiguity, department-travel alignment). The remainder are external predictors, provenance, or metadata-completeness flags (expense_type_label, entry_method, processing_lag_risk, source_id_present, ci_name_anomaly) that describe the expense or workflow rather than parts of the risk concept. Among the genuine facets, mismatch and personal/business ambiguity partly overlap in the 'misclassified/unauthorized spend' space, and department alignment is somewhat distinct, giving moderate mutual exclusivity. Exhaustiveness is low: key constitutive aspects of travel policy risk such as spending-limit/cap violations, missing-receipt/documentation compliance, disallowed expense categories, and duplicate/reimbursement fraud are not covered by any facet.
